# Hand-made assets (not generated by any script)

`circuit.svg` (in `studies/splicebert_partner_selection/`) and
`splicebert_donor_acceptor_binding.{svg,_preview.png,_grayscale.png}` are **not produced by any
script in this repo** — a grep for their names across both trees returns zero hits.

They were flagged as orphans during the 2026-07-12 cleanup and **kept anyway**, because an
orphan you can regenerate is disposable and an orphan you cannot is an original. These are the
second kind.

⚠️ If either depicts the **competing-acceptor "binding" / double-dissociation** result, it is
illustrating a claim that has been **RETRACTED (R7 — the key/value swap is an algebraic
identity)**. Check before reuse. The current circuit diagram of record is the ASCII one in
`studies/splicebert_partner_selection/MECHANISM.md`, and the figures of record are
`fig1_coupling`, `fig2_mechanism`, `fig3_circuit` (each with a `.provenance.json`).

---

## ⛔ 2026-07-13 — `splicebert_donor_acceptor_binding.svg` IS SUPERSEDED (R15)

**Do not use it. Do not extend it.**

Its title, subtitle, `<desc>`, and stage 4 all assert a **content-addressed read**:

> *"Head L3H1 performs a content-addressed read: Q·K selects the acceptor site and attention
> transports V back into the donor's residual stream."*

That is **D16**, and **D16 is retracted (R15)**. BERT's positions are absolute, so the attention
score `q_i·k_j` has **no term in the slot index j** — a (key, value) pair carried to a new slot
attracts *exactly* the attention it attracted at home (measured **9.9e-07**). "Relocation costs
2%" is a fact about the architecture, not about SpliceBERT, and the experiment could not have
come out any other way.

**Replacement: `fig_phase_circuit.svg`.** Same circuit, correct mechanism — the acceptor's address
is built from a **learned period-3 positional clock** stored in the position-embedding table, read
out by L2H15. Deleting the clock (7 of 513 Fourier bins) destroys the coupling (0.946 → 0.027);
restoring L2H15 alone recovers 36%.

---

## ✅ 2026-07-13 — the three phase figures are all GENERATED. None is a hand asset.

`fig_phase_circuit.svg` **was** hand-authored, and it is the cautionary tale this file exists for:
it had already **drifted from the data** (it printed the combs' phase mass as 0.786 where the run
says **0.794**), and its clock glyph was a **hand-drawn sawtooth** — the very artefact this thread
retired.

All three now render straight from `results/phase-lattice/fig_phase_data.json`, so **none can
drift from the result it claims to show**:

| figure | script | what it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `fig_phase_circuit` | `make_fig_phase_circuit.py` | the mechanism: clock → L2H15's address → L3H1's read → coupling |
| `fig_phase_clock` | `make_fig_phase_clock.py` | the evidence: P's spectrum, the wave in six heads, the collapse to chance, the dose-response, provenance |
| `fig_phase_wave` | `make_fig_phase_wave.py` | the readout itself — the comb **is** a cosine, and L0H11 needs **two** |
| `fig_two_carriers` | `make_fig_two_carriers.py` | P holds **two** clocks; they delete independently |

Each has a `.CAPTION.md` beside it. **The narrative lives there, not in the artwork**: the figures
are held to a few words per component, sentence case, no sentences inside the panels.

⚠️ **THE SAWTOOTH IS RETIRED. Do not re-draw the clock as a sawtooth, a comb, or a square wave.**
`R(k)` was never jagged. A period-3 signal sampled at integers carries **exactly one resolvable
sinusoid** — its second harmonic sits above Nyquist and aliases back onto the fundamental — so the
smooth curve through those points is the **exact trigonometric interpolant**, not a smoothing. The
corners were the straight-line connector. Maths in `src/gfmcd/splicing/wave.py`; tripwires in
`tests/test_wave_memorials.py`.


**Start at `figures/splicebert/README.md`** — it carries the current state of the record,
the evidence hierarchy, and the two nulls that must never be quoted as evidence (R16, Assay 1).
